$comment: Life events at work (D-068): they come up on a shift (when.on_shift), often with a coworker on shift at the same place ({name}).

events.title: Credit where it's due
events.prompt: In the meeting, {name} pitches the idea you mentioned over coffee on Tuesday. Word for word. Everyone nods. Your boss says "Brilliant."

outcomes.text: "Glad you liked my idea," you say, and smile. {name} goes red. Your boss writes your name down.

memory.text: Took my idea back from {name} in front of everyone.

outcomes.text: You try. It comes out sounding petty, and the room goes cold. {name} looks wounded; your boss looks at the clock.

memory.text: Called out {name} for stealing my idea. It went badly.

outcomes.text: You let it go. You do not let it go. You think about it in the shower for three days.

memory.text: Watched {name} take credit for my idea and said nothing.

outcomes.text: Later, by the coffee machine, {name} apologises. "I honestly forgot it was yours." You almost believe it.

memory.text: {name} and I sorted out whose idea it was.

events.title: A secret in the break room
events.prompt: {name} pulls you aside, eyes darting. "I'm interviewing somewhere else. Nobody can know. Please."

outcomes.text: You mime zipping your lips. {name} exhales like they've been holding it for a week.

memory.text: Kept {name}'s secret about the other job.

outcomes.text: "Are they hiring?" {name} laughs for the first time all week. You trade notes on the place.

memory.text: {name} told me about a job elsewhere. I asked if they had two.

outcomes.text: You mention it to your manager, "just so they're prepared." By lunch, {name} knows it was you.

memory.text: Told the boss {name} was leaving. {name} found out.

events.title: The weather in the corner office
events.prompt: Your boss has been slamming doors since nine. Someone has to take the quarterly numbers in. Everyone is looking at you.

outcomes.text: You walk in, set them down, say "Rough day?" Your boss sighs, smiles, and tells you about their kid's flu. You're a hero in the break room.

memory.text: Braved the boss on a bad day. It went fine.

outcomes.text: You get two sentences in before the door-slamming resumes, this time with you on the wrong side of it.

memory.text: Took the numbers in to the boss on a bad day. Mistake.

outcomes.text: You email the numbers with a cheerful subject line and hide behind your screen. Cowardly. Effective.

choices.label: Bring a coffee as a shield

outcomes.text: You lead with a flat white. Your boss blinks, takes it, and the storm clouds part for a full hour.

memory.text: Calmed the boss with a coffee.

events.title: Can you stay?
events.prompt: Your manager hovers by your station. "We're short tonight. Two hours, cash bonus, and I owe you one."

outcomes.text: You stay. The bonus lands, your feet ache, and your manager actually does owe you one now.

memory.text: Stayed late for a cash bonus.

outcomes.text: "I have plans," you say. Your plans are a sofa and a show. You regret nothing.
"Make it worth my while." Your manager laughs, then pays it. You've never felt more like a professional.
"Never mind," your manager says, and asks someone else. It stings more than it should.

events.title: Pastry diplomacy
events.prompt: {name} looks like they haven't slept. The whole team does. The bakery round the corner is open.

outcomes.text: You come back with a box of croissants. You are briefly the most popular person in Livéra.

memory.text: Bought the team pastries on a long morning.

outcomes.text: You slide a coffee across. {name} looks at it like it's a winning lottery ticket.
Everyone suffers in silence, together. Very professional.

events.title: The customer is always…
events.prompt: A customer is jabbing a finger at you across the counter about something that is extremely not your fault. A queue is forming.

outcomes.text: You smile until it hurts. The customer runs out of steam and leaves. The next person in the queue whispers "I'm so sorry."

memory.text: Kept my cool with a nightmare customer.

outcomes.text: You fetch the manager, who is somehow worse at this than you. Still: not your problem now.

choices.label: Tell them exactly what you think

outcomes.text: You say it. The queue applauds. Someone films it. You are a local legend for an afternoon.

memory.text: Told off a rude customer to applause.

outcomes.text: You say it. The silence afterwards is very long. Your manager asks for a word.

memory.text: Lost it with a customer at work.

events.title: Rumours from upstairs
events.prompt: {name} leans over: "Heard a title is opening up. Heard your name, too."

outcomes.text: You let yourself imagine the new title, the new desk, telling everyone. It's a nice afternoon.
"I'll believe it when I see it." You go back to work. Promotions come from the work anyway.
{name} gets vague, then vaguer. It was the guy who fixes the printer.
